Established-street house lots: A fee-simple lot carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees.

Lot character: typical Montecito lot sizes are UNVERIFIED at sub-area level — no official source read states them. The only sourced size figures are the R1 SSMUH thresholds themselves: 280 m² and 281 m².

Serviced position, as the City states it: Burnaby's 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable and a residential garbage toter fee; the detached single-family dwelling water charge is $652.33, rates carry a 5% discount if paid by the due date, and for single-family homes sewer is billed as a sewer parcel tax on the property tax notice. Montecito's established lots sit inside that City serviced system on the City's wording; servicing for any single parcel is confirmed with the City.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in Montecito is confirmed in the research; ALR status is a property-specific check through the Agricultural Land Commission, and no ALR percentage split is stated.

Flood position: the Burnaby Lake park frontage on Sperling Avenue is low and wet by the lake, but a floodplain designation for Montecito's residential streets was not confirmed in the sources read — parcel-level hazard status is UNCONFIRMED and is checked lot by lot.

No bare-land strata plan in Montecito was verified: Montecito's one strata townhouse complex, Villa Montecito (Montecito Drive / Capistrano Drive; strata plan NWS90, 75 units, counted in is a conventional building-form strata, not a bare-land strata — do not describe it as one.
The new Burnaby Lake Recreation Complex: is under construction beside Bill Copeland Sports Centre at Kensington Avenue, with City programs at Bill Copeland continuing during construction.
No rezoning proposal, assembly or development site in Montecito was verified: on a City source in the research.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Montecito

items.t: Montecito is in northeast Burnaby, south-west of Burnaby Mountain, above Lougheed Highway and Burnaby Lake; for City administrative and planning purposes it is also known as "Sperling-Broadway." "Montecito" is the GVR board sub-area name as used in the SnapStats GVR report for Burnaby. The neighbourhood sits between Kensington Avenue to the west and the Greystone / Arden side to the east, with Halifax Street to the north and Lougheed Highway to the south — exact MLS® boundary streets: UNVERIFIED.

Nearby areas: Lochdale and Parkcrest to the west, Sperling-Duthie and Burnaby Lake to the south across Lougheed Highway, Westridge and the Burnaby Mountain / SFU side to the north-east, Government Road to the south-east.

Main roads: Lougheed Highway at the south edge; Kensington Avenue, Sperling Avenue, Duthie Avenue and Halifax Street run through the neighbourhood, and Burnaby Mountain Parkway climbs from the east side to SFU. Transit anchor: Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station, an elevated Millennium Line station at Sperling Avenue and Lougheed Highway directly south of the sub-area, with bus routes 110, 134 and 144 connecting there — the 144 runs between Metrotown Station and SFU. Commute times in minutes: UNVERIFIED.

Civic anchors: Bill Copeland Sports Centre, 3676 Kensington Avenue (NHL-sized rink, 1,984 seats); Burnaby Lake Sports Complex, accessed from Kensington and Sperling Avenues (5 lit artificial turf fields plus grass fields); Burnaby Lake Regional Park wraps the lake immediately south of Lougheed Highway. The library branch serving this quadrant is the Temporary Cameron Branch at The City of Lougheed Shopping Centre, 9855 Austin Ave; the permanent Cameron replacement status is UNVERIFIED. Nearest hospital: Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St.
Schools: SD41 (Burnaby) has no middle-school tier — elementary K–7, secondary 8–12 — and catchments are address-based. Every other address needs its own locator run.

Shopping: there is no enclosed mall or town centre inside the sub-area; Burnaby's plan framework designates Brentwood (west) and Lougheed (east) as town centres, with Kensington Square at Hastings and Kensington as the local plaza.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Montecito

items.t: Subdivision + servicing — confirmed instrument (fresh check, Nov 2, 2026): Burnaby's servicing bylaw is the Burnaby Subdivision Control and Development Servicing Bylaw — the former Burnaby Subdivision Control Bylaw 1971 as renamed and amended by Amendment Bylaw No. 14667 (2024), in force September 30, 2024. Its s. 4A requires parcels created by subdivision to conform to the Zoning Bylaw for the zone, and s. 5A lists the works and services a subdivision can be required to provide (highways and lanes, water, sewage and drainage systems connected to the City's systems). The City's Servicing Improvements Guide applies the updated bylaw to developments of four or more primary dwelling units on a residential lot, including cash-in-lieu contributions to curbs, sidewalks, lanes, boulevards, street trees, streetlights and road widening. Confirm the parcel-level requirement with the City's Engineering Department before pricing a split.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Montecito ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Check the parcel on ALC mapping before applying any of this.

The City does not call this area Montecito (2026 documents): for Burnaby administrative and planning purposes the same ground is "Sperling-Broadway" — a buyer reading City plans, the 2050 OCP maps or facility pages under "Montecito" alone will miss material filed under the planning name.

Burnaby replaced its entire zoning bylaw and renamed its servicing bylaw within two years: the Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815) took effect July 1, 2026 and repealed the 1965 bylaw, and the Subdivision Control Bylaw was renamed the Subdivision Control and Development Servicing Bylaw effective September 30, 2024 — any older guide citing the 1965 zoning bylaw, or quoting pre-2024 servicing rules for a 4+ unit project, is out of date.

The new OCP outranks the old plans (adopted December 9, 2025): the Burnaby 2050 OCP takes precedence over older community-plan land use maps where they conflict, so a density assumption carried from an older community plan for a Montecito lot is not safe until it is re-checked against the 2050 map.

Half the Halifax "condo pocket" cannot be bought: the strata Ambassador (1987) stands beside Montecito Towers (7360 / 7376 Halifax, built 1972, 136 units), which is purpose-built rental only — the pocket a land buyer might read as an assembly target is one strata corporation plus a rental complex, not lots.

The sports fields were closed most of 2026 and are back: Burnaby Lake Sports Complex Fields 1 and 2 were closed for turf upgrades scheduled May to September 2026 and were listed OPEN again in the City's October 29, 2026 field-status update, while the new Burnaby Lake Recreation Complex is under construction beside Bill Copeland — the amenity story on the area's south-west edge is mid-build, not finished.

faq.a: In northeast Burnaby, south-west of Burnaby Mountain, between Kensington Avenue and the Greystone side, above Lougheed Highway and Burnaby Lake. The City also calls the area "Sperling-Broadway" for planning purposes, and it is a GVR MLS® sub-area within the City of Burnaby (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: Which schools serve a Montecito address?
faq.a: It depends on the address. Montecito Elementary (K–7), 2176 Duthie Ave, is the in-area SD41 school and École Sperling Elementary (K–7) sits at the area's south-west side; catchments are address-based and must be checked in the SD41 locator.

faq.q: Is there SkyTrain service in Montecito?
faq.a: The station is at the area's south edge: Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station (Millennium Line) sits at Sperling Avenue and Lougheed Highway, with buses 110, 134 and 144 connecting there — the 144 links the station to Metrotown and SFU.

faq.q: What is there to do at Burnaby Lake?
faq.a: Burnaby Lake Regional Park is a wildlife sanctuary with walking trails, viewing towers and docks, a Nature House, and a rowing course with a pavilion and public canoe launch at the Burnaby Lake Sports Complex; the sports complex itself has 5 lit artificial turf fields.

faq.q: How is the market in Montecito?
faq.a: Quiet in September 2026: 2 detached sales against 20 active listings (10% sales ratio) and no attached sales on 12 listings, so the attached sales ratio is not applicable. Burnaby-wide, the median detached sale price was $1,825,000 that month (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: Is there a vacant-lot subdivision I can buy into in Montecito?
faq.a: No verified one. Montecito is an established neighbourhood — land trades as built house lots, one strata apartment building, one strata townhouse complex and rental product. No presale lot offering was verified.

faq.q: What can a Montecito house lot actually become?
faq.a: Under the R1 SSMUH district, 3 units on a lot up to 280 m², 4 units on a larger lot, and 6 units only on a lot of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop — and a lot with two or more primary units may be stratified. Measure the lot and run the 400 m test before pricing any multiplex value.

faq.q: Can I subdivide a large lot here, and what servicing will the City require?
faq.a: Subdivision runs under the Burnaby Subdivision Control and Development Servicing Bylaw (the 1971 bylaw as renamed by Amendment Bylaw No. 14667, in force September 30, 2024): new parcels must conform to the Zoning Bylaw, and the bylaw's works-and-services list covers highways, water, sewer and drainage connections; developments of four or more primary units also face the City's servicing-improvements regime, including cash-in-lieu items. Get the Engineering pre-application answer for the specific lot first.

faq.q: Is there any bare-land strata in Montecito?
faq.a: None verified. The area's strata townhouse complex, Villa Montecito, is a conventional strata (plan NWS90) — you buy a strata townhouse with a Form B, not a bare-land lot. If a bare-land strata lot were offered here, it would still be strata tenure in full: fees, bylaws and Form B diligence.

The City's utility wording puts established homes on annual water and sewer billing (detached water charge $652.33 for 2026, sewer as a parcel tax for single-family homes) — confirm the specific parcel's connections and any servicing upgrade the Subdivision Control and Development Servicing Bylaw will require for your project.
